title: dashboard telemetry evaporation: RCA and hotpatch for missing tenant metrics & span gaps
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Several enterprise customers reported missing dashboard tiles and incomplete traces during an incident window (2026-02-28 03:00-06:30 UTC). This ticket tracks the RCA and immediate hotpatch to restore telemetry coverage and provide a safe backfill path. The behavior is reproducible on tenant read-paths after a high-traffic compaction event combined with an index snapshot GC. We need a low-risk patch to surface fallback metrics in the Console, run a controlled rehydration for affected tenants, and add guardrails to prevent future evaporation of short-lived metric references.
impact_summary: Customer-facing dashboards showed blank tiles for up to 3.5 hours; alerting for several SLOs did not fire because metric references were collected; traces for long-running requests lost tail spans for ~40% of sampled requests. Impacted customers include two Dedicated tenants and multiple Hosted customers using high-cardinality telemetry. Severity: customer escalations opened with Support and Solutions Engineering.
reproduction_steps: 1) Load a tenant with high-cardinality metrics and rapid series churn (simulate 10k unique series over 30 mins).
2) Trigger a storage compaction + index snapshot rotation (replicate our nightly compaction code path).
3) Push sample traces for requests that overlap compaction; observe post-compaction queries returning missing metric series and truncated traces.
4) Query Console live panels for the tenant and observe blank tiles and 'no data' states despite ingestion logs showing writes during the window.
root_cause: An interaction between the index snapshot GC policy and the console's adaptive index window selector caused recently-rotated index shards to be marked as compactable while the live query planner still referenced them. The storage compactor removed lightweight metric reference entries (short-lived series) earlier than the console fallback expected. Separately, trace ingestion partition mapping had a sparse-shard edge case: when spans for a trace landed across a compaction boundary, the reassembly lookup failed due to an off-by-one partition bucket calculation introduced in runtime-1.45. These two failures combined to produce missing dashboard tiles and truncated traces.
mitigation_and_hotpatch_steps: 1) Hotpatch the Console server (console-2026.03-hotfixA): add a fallback that serves metrics from the last-known index snapshot if the adaptive window returns empty, with a visible banner notifying users that data may be delayed.
2) Deploy a temporary retention bump for index snapshot GC (storage-rollout-urgent): extend safeRetentionWindow from 10m -> 60m for affected tenants to avoid immediate reaping during high churn.
3) Push trace reassembly fix (runtime-1.45.1 patch): correct partition bucket calculation and add unit tests that simulate compaction boundary spans.
4) Kick off controlled rehydration job that replays compacted lightweight references for impacted tenants for the 3.5h window (rehydration-job-2026-03-03).
5) Notify impacted customers with timeline, mitigations, and expected resolution ETA; coordinate Solutions Eng for post-recovery validation.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows non-empty fallback metrics for previously blank tiles within 30 minutes of hotpatch deploy.
Backfill/rehydration completes for the incident window and dashboard tiles show aligned values (minor differences allowed due to aggregation).
Trace tail-span recovery confirmed with sampling parity >= 95% vs baseline for replayed traces.
Regression tests added for index window selector and trace partitioning; CI green for runtime-1.45.1 and console hotpatch.
Customer confirmation from at least 2 affected accounts that dashboards/traces are restored.
rollout_plan: Canary deploy console hotpatch to eu-west-1 and us-east-1 with 15% traffic for 15 minutes; monitor tile resurfacing and error rates.
If stable, roll to 100% over 30 minutes.
Apply storage retention bump via config-rollout for the two Dedicated tenants immediately, then evaluate system-wide need.
Deploy runtime trace fix to dedicated pools first, observe reassembly success, then push to hosted pools.
Run rehydration job in low-priority worker pool to avoid impacting production ingestion; monitor ingestion lag and compute usage.
